mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals labor market overheating, which historically precedes Fed tightening and higher input costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for two consecutive months signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which increases discount rates and erodes real earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both > 3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses corporate profits and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall > 1% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for eight consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which historically precedes higher wage pressures and Fed tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA for eight consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.2%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and weaker consumer spending, which reduces demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
